name: ark
summary: a git-aware project archiver that separates code, re-downloadable dependencies, and irreplaceable local files. bundles history, preserves uncommitted work, and verifies backups with SHA-256 manifests. python standard library, with a web UI and MCP tools.
problem: Large project folders mix source code, replaceable dependencies, and files that cannot be downloaded again. Ark organizes those differences into a reviewable archive before a project is removed or moved.
highlights: Git-aware preservation: Save repository history as a Git bundle and preserve uncommitted work as a patch. Detect nested repositories and problematic gitlinks.
File classification: Separate re-downloadable caches and dependencies from locally generated data, outputs, and other irreplaceable files. Ambiguous items are saved and flagged.
Integrity checks: SHA-256 manifests verify the archive after creation or transport, with restore hints explaining what needs to be fetched again.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Scan the project and review its classification.
- Inspect or adjust the archive plan.
- Build the archive with history, patches, and preserved files.
- Verify the archive and review the restoration checklist.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: Python standard-library tools power the CLI, web interface, and MCP server. The archive includes a runbook, restore hints, classification plan, and integrity manifests.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: Classification uses heuristics and Git information. Review the plan before deleting source files; Ark creates a local archive and does not upload it or download replacement dependencies.
